input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion, each of the
four flows is fully operable with keyboard alone — focus is managed correctly in
modals, no control is unreachable, and focus indicators are consistent. This is
the code deliverable of the keyboard accessibility conformance strategy and the
foundation for the updated conformance documentation.

## Scope

- Remediate every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report for the
  four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission), including focus loss in modals and unreachable
  controls.
- Implement correct focus management in modals and dialogs used by the audited
  flows: focus moves into the modal on open, is trapped while open, returns to
  the triggering control on close, and standard dismiss keys work.
- Make every interactive control in the audited flows reachable and operable by
  keyboard alone.
- Apply a consistent, visible focus indicator style across all interactive
  controls in the audited flows.
- Verify the fixes do not regress non-audited behavior of the affected
  components.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
  and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, When it is operated end to end with keyboard
  input only, Then every step completes successfully with no focus traps and no
  unreachable controls — measured by a keyboard-only walkthrough of the flow.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, When operated end to end with keyboard input
  only, Then every step completes with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls — measured by a keyboard-only walkthrough of the flow.
- Given the model deployment flow, When operated end to end with keyboard input
  only, Then every step completes with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls — measured by a keyboard-only walkthrough of the flow.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, When operated end to end with keyboard
  input only, Then every step completes with no focus traps and no unreachable
  controls — measured by a keyboard-only walkthrough of the flow.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited flows is
  remediated in code, or explicitly dispositioned with rationale.
- Focus indicators are visible on all interactive controls in the audited flows
  and use a consistent style — measured by inspection across the four flows.
- Automated accessibility checks covering keyboard and focus rules pass on the
  audited flows with no new violations introduced — measured by the check run
  on the changed builds.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the keyboard
  remediation of the four flows in this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the consistent focus-indicator work in this epic; kept in
  the same epic as HLR-1 because both concern the same flows, component, and
  team, and a split would audit the same surfaces twice.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and docs statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation to
reflect the state of the Dashboard after the keyboard accessibility remediation
of the four core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
pipeline run submission). It delivers the published VPAT conformance statement
and the product documentation accessibility statement that public-sector
customers require before renewal. This epic starts after the keyboard
remediation work is implemented, because the conformance claims must describe
the fixed state and be technically reviewed against it.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) conformance report
  to reflect the remediated keyboard operability and focus-indicator state of
  the four audited flows.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Republish both the VPAT and the accessibility statement at their official
  product locations.
- Ensure conformance claims are scoped accurately: claims cover the four
  remediated flows and do not assert keyboard operability for flows or controls
  outside them, and do not assert screen-reader conformance beyond what the
  keyboard fixes deliver.
- Obtain and record technical review of the updated documentation against the
  implemented behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the remediated state of the four audited flows
  and republished at the product's official conformance location — measured by
  the published document reflecting the fixed behavior.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated and republished
  to reflect the fixed state — measured by the published statement.
- Technical review is completed and recorded: a reviewer confirms each
  conformance claim in the VPAT and accessibility statement matches the
  implemented keyboard behavior of the audited flows — measured by a completed
  review sign-off.
- No conformance claim in the published documents asserts capabilities outside
  the remediated scope (the four audited flows; keyboard operability and focus
  indicators) — measured by a claim-by-claim check against the remediation
  scope.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review — fully covered by this epic.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Parent strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

**Triage assessment:** Not below-threshold. Although the code scope is confined to
one component (Dashboard) with a fully enumerated defect list, the strategy spans
two architecturally distinct work streams — code implementation (keyboard
remediation, HLR-1/HLR-2) and substantive documentation authoring (VPAT and
product docs accessibility statement, HLR-3). Per the multiple-work-streams escape
condition, the strategy proceeds to full decomposition. Not docs-only: Dashboard
requires code changes.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and docs statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001: Keyboard accessibility remediation (Dashboard)"] --> E002["E002: VPAT and docs accessibility statement (Documentation)"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by ALL Implementation epics) | The conformance documentation must describe the fixed state; it cannot be authored or technically reviewed until the keyboard remediation is implemented. Docs-authoring priority exception applies: E002 keeps P2 (strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2) and does not push priority onto E001. |

No other edges: E001 is the only code epic (single component, single team, one
logical change — the audit-enumerated keyboard remediation across the four flows —
so it stays one epic per Epic Boundary Rule 2; the four flows share the same
component, team, and change type, and no Investigation epics are needed because
the strategy states there are no open questions and the audit report enumerates
the exact defects per flow).

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E001 | Consistent focus indicators — same component, team, and UI surfaces as HLR-1; one mechanical remediation pass, splitting would audit the same flows twice |
| HLR-3 | P2 | E002 | VPAT and docs accessibility statement update, republish, technical review |

Full coverage: HLR-1, HLR-2, HLR-3 all mapped; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted Teams
  table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, no
  Non-Functional Requirements, and the Affected Components section is a bare list
  without per-component change descriptions or owner teams. Decomposition proceeded
  from the HLR table, problem statement, and open-questions section.
- **Team assignment inferred**: the Dashboard owner (RHOAI Dashboard) is taken from
  the architecture context file; the Documentation owner (RHOAI Documentation) is
  assumed, since the strategy names no docs team. Human verification recommended.
- **Priority observation**: the problem statement ties both deliverables to public-
  sector customer renewals, yet HLR-3 is P2. This is consistent with the
  docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority Normal → P2), but the
  renewal pressure may justify elevating the documentation work at planning time.
- **Scope boundary**: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require and flows outside the four audited ones are out of scope per the
  strategy; the conformance documentation must not claim beyond the remediated
  scope.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; both epics are
internal to the platform teams.
